bull_bear.body: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion (oral solids, injectables) and inorganic M&A in niche segments. Dividend: INR 1 final + INR 2 special (total INR 3/share). Strong FCF (INR 958cr) supports aggressive growth capex without debt.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) API Price Volatility: Cephalosporin and bulk API prices remain below peak levels, pressuring API segment profitability. 2) Geopolitical/Crude: Inflation in solvents/raw materials (though largely pass-through). 3) Execution Risk: Delays in EU commercialization or Zambia facility commissioning. 4) Regulatory: Schedule M implementation pace and inspection outcomes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and pragmatic. Acknowledged FY26 as 'transitional' with H1 challenges but emphasized strong Q4 momentum. Clear focus on long-term value creation via regulated markets over short-term trade generic scale. Transparent on API losses and path to recovery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Trade Generics business was consciously shrunk to fix working capital cycles, not due to lack of demand; it is now a small, profitable niche. The EUR 200mn EU contract is for an established molecule with predictable volumes, de-risking the ramp-up. The Zambia deal includes a transition from export (FY27-28) to local manufacturing (FY29+), locking in long-term sovereign demand.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Objects-of-the-offer table shows the IPO proceeds fully deployed as on June 30, 2026, with the unutilized amount shown as "-" against every object.
- Stated objects and amounts (INR Cr, offer document = utilization): repayment of borrowings of Akums 159.91; repayment of borrowings of subsidiaries 227.09; funding incremental working capital 55.00; pursuing inorganic growth initiatives through acquisitions 30.18; general corporate purposes 170.00.
- The Rs 56 Crore Oriflame purchase is presented as in line with the stated inorganic-growth strategy of improving positioning and augmenting margins.
- Managing Directors state they "remain committed to creating long term shareholder value".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: CDMO: Rev INR 3,485cr (+8.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 467cr (+2.9%); Q4 Rev INR 952cr (+13.4%), EBITDA INR 137cr (+54.9%). Domestic Branded: Rev INR 446cr (+2.9%), EBITDA INR 90cr (+17%); Q4 Rev declined 1.5%. Int'l Branded: Rev flat at INR 143cr, EBITDA +32.3% to INR 36cr; Q4 Rev -9.7%. Trade Generics: Rev INR 100cr (-13.2%), EBITDA turned positive at INR -10cr (vs -28cr); Q4 EBITDA +INR 1.4cr. API: Rev INR 184cr (-15.9%), EBITDA loss narrowed to INR -40cr (vs -44cr); Q4 loss widened to INR -12cr due to mix/volume.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck frames Akums as its clients' "preferred manufacturing partner", saying the consistent performance of CDMO "showcases healthy demand environment as well as our clients' trust in Akums".
- "More than Two Decades' Legacy of Expertise, Experience & Trust" — incorporated April 2004, with the deck splitting its history into Build (2004), Strengthen (2010), Accelerate (2021) and 2026 phases.
- Five stated business verticals — CDMO, Domestic Branded Formulation, International Branded Formulation, API and Trade Generics — with CDMO at 82.6% share in revenue in Q1 FY27.
- Deck states management "remain[s] confident of the structural attractiveness of our chosen geographies" for the international branded formulations business.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition rationale] Deck cites favourable Indian cosmetics market dynamics — rising disposable incomes, urbanization, demand for sustainable products, easy accessibility and rise of influencer marketing — as drivers behind the Oriflame deal.
- [Inorganic history] Akums acquired Parabolic Drugs to venture into API, and launched Akumentis to venture into branded formulations, per the milestone timeline.
- [Input prices] Deck states "API prices saw an increase in Q1 after constant decline in the last 3 quarters. Although volatility remains high in Q2."
- [Definitions] Deck defines EBITDA as excluding other income, and separately reports an "EBITDA (including other income)" line — the two bases are not interchangeable.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: CDMO model is cost-plus percentage margin; absolute profits fluctuate with API input costs. Recent API price hikes (single high-digits) benefit absolute margins despite soft YoY comparison. Gross margins supported by shift to complex dosage forms and regulated markets. Operating leverage from capacity utilization driving EBITDA expansion.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: CDMO double-digit volume growth expected in H1 FY27; Domestic Formulations to grow at/above IPM (high single/low double digit); International Formulations to return to double-digit growth. Margins: CDMO margins to sustain ~13-14%; API losses to reduce sizably but may remain negative for full year FY27. Order Inflow: Zambia supplies commence Q2 FY27; EU commercial supplies from FY28. Capex: INR 300cr targeted for FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Zambia: $25mn per annum for FY27 & FY28 (supplies from India), followed by local manufacturing ramp-up from FY29. EU CDMO: EUR 35mn per annum for 6 years (till 2032), commencing FY28. Domestic CDMO: Strong pipeline with 10+ products for European markets.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Zambia JV: $45mn total capex (51% Akums), local production from FY29 targeting $200mn market. 2) EU Regulated Markets: Plant 2 accredited, dossier filing underway for 10+ products, commercial supply FY28. 3) Injectables: New facility ramping up (teens utilization), expected significant contribution in FY27. 4) Inorganic M&A: Evaluating niche business acquisitions using strong cash reserves.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Akums navigated a challenging H1 FY26 to deliver strong Q4 recovery, driven by double-digit CDMO volume growth and the turning of Trade Generics EBITDA positive, while setting up significant optionality via a $25mn/year Zambia sovereign contract and EU commercial supplies starting FY28. The key inflection is the expected sharp reduction in API losses and the transition from domestic dependency to high-margin regulated market exports.

open.item: European audit of API facility expected in the upcoming quarter (Q1 FY27), to unlock regulated-market opportunities at improved realization

Zambia supplies of ~USD 25 million (~INR 230 crore) from Indian facilities expected to commence by end of Q2 FY27, flowing into CDMO revenue at CDMO-similar margins
CDMO margins expected to sustain a similar profile to current (~13-14%) into FY27
API losses (~negative INR 40 crore for three consecutive years) expected to come down sharply in FY27, though full year likely still negative; monthly EBITDA positive is the aspiration
Domestic branded formulation (Akumentis) expected to grow at above-IPM / double-digit top-line rates in FY27 driven by new launches, brand building and field-force productivity
International branded formulation expected to return to double-digit growth in FY27 after a flat FY26, with margin profile sustained (~28% in Q4)
FY26 capex was INR 222 crore; FY27 capex targeted at INR 300 crore, partly for oral solid facility expansion
Expanding oral solids facility to accommodate 20%+ volume growth over two quarters; part of FY27 capex will go here
Effective tax rate ~32% currently; management expects to build in ~29% going forward, normalizing toward 25% once loss-making entities (API, trade generics) turn profitable
Patented Triple Hair topical hair-loss product to be launched in 2027 for the Indian market, expanding dermatology portfolio
European CDMO contract (Plant 2, EU GMP approved Jan) to commence commercial supplies in FY28; expected ~EUR 35 million on a MAT basis annually through 2032 at similar/high-teen margins
By FY28 export CDMO (Europe EUR 35m MAT + Zambia USD 25m) could be ~15%-plus of CDMO revenues (~INR 680 crore), lifting base CDMO margins as both contracts hit full swing
Zambia local manufacturing facility (Akums 51%, USD 45m total) targeted to start commercial production in CY2029/FY29-FY30; India supply contract ceases after FY28
Over the next 2-3 years, target to have 8-10 global CDMO customers (Indian or European/global players) served across oral solids, injectables and niche products
Cash and equivalents of INR 1,682 crore to be deployed primarily for organic/inorganic growth; evaluating niche acquisitions (MDIs, oncology injectables, large molecules) though valuations must fit
